Question_text: Fig. 1.1 shows a model of the human arm. The rubber band represents the muscle that moves part of the arm XY up. A mass is suspended from XY, as shown in Fig. 1.2. The weight of section XY is negligible and the model is at rest.
image:
Fig. 1.1 is a diagram showing a model of a human arm. It consists of a rigid bar labeled XY, pivoted at one end (X). A rubber band connects a point on the rigid bar (near X) to an elevated point above the pivot, representing a muscle. The other end Y is free.
Fig. 1.2 is a diagram showing the same human arm model as Fig. 1.1, but with a mass suspended from end Y. The rubber band is stretched. Dimensions are given: the distance from the pivot X to the point where the rubber band attaches is 2.0 cm, and the distance from the pivot X to where the mass is suspended (Y) is 16 cm. The labels 'rubber band', 'pivot', 'X', 'Y', and 'mass' are present.

Parts.part_text: State two ways in which the dimensions of the rubber band change as the mass is added to section XY.
State the form of energy stored in the stretched rubber band.
State the principle of moments.
Explain why the force that the rubber band exerts on section XY is larger than the weight of the mass.
The mass suspended from section XY in Fig. 1.2 has a weight of 4.0N. Calculate the force that the rubber band exerts on section XY.
Explain how your answer to (b)(iii) is different if the weight of section XY is not negligible.

Wind energy is a form of renewable energy. State the name of one other form of renewable energy.
